messages:
infra-monitor-bot: Alert: Unusual billing spike detected for project/redwood-prod-us-west — spend rate +340% vs rolling baseline. Trigger: gpu-ec2-spot-asg. Link: https://billing.redwood.internal/alerts/1715001234

mike: seeing this in the dashboard now. looks like autoscaler launched a bunch of p4d instances instead of our usual a100-backed fleet. anyone touching launch templates in the last 24h? :eyes:

anya: I pushed a change to autoscaler mappings this morning (trying to add newer spot families). I thought I scoped it to canary, but maybe it applied to prod. digging in.

raj: quick command: aws autoscaling describe-auto-scaling-groups --auto-scaling-group-names gpu-ec2-spot-asg | jq '.AutoScalingGroups[].Instances[].InstanceType' -> returns 40x p4d.24xlarge

lina: cost-ops: any rough burn estimate? this many p4d nodes for 2 hours could be painful.

cost-ops: ballpark: p4d.24x ~ $32/hr (on-demand equivalent) -> 40 nodes * $32 * 2h ~= $2560 just for compute delta. with attached GPUs + EBS + data egress ~ $4k. But spot behaviour + capacity reclamation made it churn; total incremental today may be ~$28k. sending invoice breakout now.

mike: thanks. the bigger issue is they kept relaunching — health checks failing and CA kept growing the pool. root cause might be a mismatch between node startup script image and driver versions. when k8s node fails kubelet it gets terminated and CA spins new ones -> runaway.

anya: reproducing: launch-template prod-gpu-template v12 has InstanceType override map that reads from env var GPU_FAMILY. I accidentally set default to p4d when testing new job types. I also widened the ASG max from 80 -> 400 in the same PR (for capacity testing). bad combo. 

raj: suggestions: 1) immediately suspend scaling processes on the ASG, 2) set desired to safe baseline, 3) rollback launch-template to v11. I can run the suspend now if folks agree.

mike: do it. also open emergency revert PR and pin node-selector on current k8s daemonset to avoid new pods scheduling to any remaining p4d nodes.

raj: running: aws autoscaling suspend-processes --auto-scaling-group-name gpu-ec2-spot-asg 

infra-monitor-bot: ASG suspend-processes OK — suspended processes: Launch, Terminate, HealthCheck. ASG desired set to 12 -> previous desired 120.

lina: rolling back launch-template to v11 now. PR: https://git.internal/redwood/infra/launch-templates/pull/482 (emergency revert).

anya: confirmed - reverted default GPU_FAMILY to a100, restored maxNodes 80. Will follow up with a post-mortem. Sorry everyone.

mike: follow-ups: - cost-ops to file chargeback + update forecast, - anya to add stricter prod-only guardrails (require two approvals for changes that touch launch-templates or ASG limits), - infra to add an autoscaler safety circuit (cap on new GPU vCPU per 10m).

cost-ops: filing ticket now and flagging finance for provisional credit request. ETA for full billing reconciliation 48h.

anya: posting short incident blurb for #all-hands and adding a prevention checklist to infra runbook. Also will add pre-deploy integration test that validates launch-template defaults against allowed-families list.

mike: good. quick ops note: if anyone needs to check which nodes were affected: kubectl get nodes -l node-type=gpu | grep p4d ; and aws ec2 describe-instances --filters 'Name=instance-type,Values=p4d.24xlarge' 'Name=tag:Cluster,Values=redwood-prod'

lina: leaving a reminder: we should convert some steady baseline into reserved/dedicated capacity for A100 families to avoid future spot surprises. if we had more reserved a100 commit, autoscaler wouldn't have had to pick p4d spot options for urgent capacity. add to backlog.

mike: +1. I'll sync with product on Dedicated commitments during SRE review next week. For now, incident closed from an operational POV — monitoring trending back to baseline.

infra-monitor-bot: Resolved: billing rate returning to baseline after ASG correction. Alert closed.
